{"answers":[{"question_id":"Q004_ferritin_like_functional_divergence","answer":"SCOPe supports remote common ancestry with functional divergence among these proteins. In release 2.08, Ferritin (a.25.1.1; SUNID 47241), Ribonucleotide reductase-like (a.25.1.2; 47253), and Manganese catalase (T-catalase) (a.25.1.3; 100951) are separate families within the Ferritin-like superfamily (a.25.1; 47240), Ferritin-like fold (a.25; 47239), and All alpha proteins class (a; 46456).

The shared superfamily expresses probable evolutionary relatedness, stronger than sharing a fold alone. Fold describes structural topology; class describes secondary-structure composition. Families represent closer evolutionary relationships, but even family membership does not guarantee identical chemistry. The conserved scaffold is an alpha-helical bundle associated with a binuclear metal-binding site; SCOPe explicitly annotates a bimetal-ion centre within the bundle.

Different functions are compatible with diversification of this scaffold: ferritins support iron storage and mineralization, with ferroxidase activity in appropriate subunits; class I ribonucleotide reductase R2 proteins generate or maintain the radical cofactor used by the catalytic partner for nucleotide reduction; manganese catalases use a dimanganese centre to disproportionate hydrogen peroxide. The Ribonucleotide reductase-like family also includes desaturases and monooxygenase subunits, so its name must not be interpreted as assigning ribonucleotide-reductase activity to every member.

Neither iron versus manganese specificity nor substrate, catalytic mechanism, radical chemistry, or oligomeric assembly should be transferred solely from this classification. A remote relative may provide a template for the conserved structural core, but not automatically for active-site geometry or functional loops. Functional assignment requires sequence/profile evidence, comparison of metal ligands and surrounding residues, experimentally established metal occupancy and biochemical activity, and relevant partner or assembly information. Representatives should therefore be selected for the intended structural or functional comparison, rather than treating one superfamily member as functionally representative of all three families.","evidence_used":["Pretrained model knowledge","mcp__scope__search_scop","mcp__scope__get_scop_node","mcp__scope__list_scop_children","/api/v1/releases/current","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sccs/a.25.1","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sccs/a.25.1/parents","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sccs/a.25.1/children?limit=100","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/47240","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/47240/annotations","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/47253/children?limit=30"]}]}
